title: Flights Bought Apart From the Holiday in a Corrected Declaration
content:
Flights the traveller bought apart from the packaged holiday are added to the prepaid cost when a
declaration on the Travel Protection Plans is corrected. The booking is the air booking that departs on the
first date of the journey, held under the Air Ticket Fare Brands, and it counts only where the operator's ledger
for the packaged holiday held under the Vacation Package Products carries no flight component of its own.

## The three readings

1. Where an air booking departing on the first date of the journey stands ticketed and the holiday's ledger
   carries no flight component, what has been prepaid for flights bought apart from the holiday is the money
   paid on that booking.
2. Where such a booking stands held rather than ticketed and the holiday's ledger carries no flight component,
   it is the fares charged on that booking.
3. In every other case nothing is added for flights bought apart from the holiday.

## Points of judgement

Where the holiday's ledger carries a charge for a flight component, nothing is added for flights bought apart,
whatever the standing of the air booking, because the flights are already inside the holiday's own cost. Where
the ledger carries no flight component but the air booking stands refunded or cancelled rather than ticketed or
held, the third reading answers and nothing is added. The money paid on a ticketed booking and the fares charged
on a held booking are different figures on the carrier's record, and each reading takes the one it names.
